angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 118,269 km at 40.11 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 24.9338 +/- 0.0204 mas (same row, RUWE 1.13): 40.11 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.17 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Muirhead et al. 2012, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-42 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012arXiv1201.2189M/abstract): 118,269 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.13 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Muirhead et al. 2012, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-42 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012arXiv1201.2189M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3068 +/- 174 K from Muirhead et al. 2012, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-42 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012arXiv1201.2189M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Muirhead et al. 2012, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-42 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012arXiv1201.2189M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-42.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.091, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
